question: How do golden tests differ from regular evaluation metrics in a regression suite?
options: Golden tests only apply to the greeting behavior
Golden tests use a different LLM model for evaluation
Golden tests run faster than evaluation metrics
Golden tests are pass/fail guards on critical behaviors that must never break, while evaluation metrics produce scores on a scale
explanation: Evaluation metrics produce numeric scores (e.g., 4.2/5 for tone) that track quality trends. Golden tests are binary pass/fail — if the agent gives medical advice (a golden test behavior), it fails regardless of other scores. Golden test failures should block deployment because they represent critical safety or business guardrails.

question: Why is a regression threshold of 0.5 points recommended on a 5-point scale rather than flagging any score drop?
options: Score drops below 0.5 are impossible with LLM-based evaluation
The evaluation framework rounds all scores to the nearest 0.5
LLM-based scoring has natural variance, so small drops (e.g., 0.2 points) may just be noise rather than real regressions
A 0.5 threshold ensures exactly 10% of runs trigger regression warnings
explanation: LLM-based evaluation is inherently variable — the same conversation might score 4.2 on one run and 4.0 on another. A threshold of 0.5 filters out this natural variance so you only flag meaningful quality drops. Running evaluations multiple times and averaging can further reduce noise.

question: When should you update the baseline rather than investigating a detected regression?
options: Whenever the regression check fails to save time
Only when the score drops are the result of intentional changes, such as deliberately modifying the greeting style
After every deployment to keep the baseline current
When the regression threshold exceeds 1.0 points
explanation: The baseline represents a known-good state. If you intentionally changed the agent's behavior (e.g., redesigned the greeting) and a related score shifts, that is expected — update the baseline to reflect the new intentional behavior. If you did not intend the change, the regression is a bug that needs investigation and fixing.
